newsitem.title: FRANCE: De Silguy sees agreement on EMU pact in Amsterdam.
newsitem.headline: De Silguy sees agreement on EMU pact in Amsterdam.

text.p: European Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said on Thursday he believed Europe would be able to reach a deal at a summit in Amsterdam next week on a stability pact aimed at limiting budget deficits under monetary union.

It would do so by making more explicit reference to the need to coordinate economic policies across Europe and fight to reduce unemployment, he told reporters before a meeting with French President Jacques Chirac.

"I think it will be possible to have an Amsterdam solution based on the definitive and formal acceptance of the stability pact...and secondly to give more explicit reference to coordination of economic policy and employment in using the provisions of the treaty, particularly (articles) 103 and 102a," he said.
France's new Socialist-led government is seeking a better balance in Europe between budget discipline and price stability on one hand and the need for growth and jobs on the other.

It says it is seeking to apply fully the Maastricht treaty which makes provision for intensified policy coordination and stresses growth and jobs alongside budget discipline and price stability as necessary for the success of monetary union.
